subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Ordering paragraphs of a narrative essay and the stages of essay writing
outcomes: Order jumbled paragraphs into a narrative essay using linking words
Put the eight stages of essay writing in the correct order

tf.s: The first stage of essay writing is making sure you understand the title.
tf.why: You need to know what the essay is about before you start.

tf.s: Proofreading means reading through your work to correct mistakes.
tf.why: Proofreading catches spelling and grammar errors.

tf.s: You should hand in your first draft without changing it.
tf.why: A first draft always needs changes; nobody writes a perfect essay at first.

tf.s: A draft is a piece of writing that is not yet in its final form.
tf.why: Drafts are revised before the final version.

tf.s: Linking words like 'He' can refer back to someone already mentioned, like 'the chef'.
tf.why: This helps you see which paragraph comes next.

tf.s: You should proofread before you write your first draft.
tf.why: Proofreading comes near the end, after the final draft.

tf.s: In 'A Nightmare Meal', paragraph E gives the general background.
tf.why: The background usually comes first, so E starts the essay.

tf.s: Planning comes after writing the final draft.
tf.why: You plan before you write any draft.

tf.s: Handing in the essay is the last stage of essay writing.
tf.why: You hand in only after proofreading.

tf.s: To revise means to throw your essay away and start a new topic.
tf.why: To revise means to improve and change your draft.

boxes.q: What is the first stage of essay writing?
boxes.why: Start by understanding what the title asks.

boxes.q: What is the last stage of essay writing?
boxes.why: You hand in the essay at the end.

boxes.q: What comes straight after the first draft?
boxes.why: You revise the first draft to improve it.

boxes.q: Which paragraph gives the general background?
boxes.why: Paragraph E sets the scene first.

boxes.q: Which paragraph comes last in the essay?
boxes.why: The order is E, C, B, D, A, F.

boxes.q: In the linking words, who does 'He' refer to?

boxes.why: A draft can still be changed.
You collect ideas, then plan them.

boxes.q: What kind of essay is 'A Nightmare Meal'?
boxes.why: It tells a story of a bad meal.

hunt.q: Writing not yet in final form

o: A piece of writing that is not yet in its final form
mcq.why: A draft is an early version that you improve.

mcq.q: Which is the correct order of the essay paragraphs?
o: E, C, B, D, A, F
A, B, C, D, E, F
F, A, D, B, C, E
E, A, B, C, D, F
mcq.why: Paragraph E gives background and F ends the story.
Revise, final draft, proofread, hand in.

mcq.q: How many stages of essay writing are there in the lesson?
mcq.why: Understand, gather, plan, first draft, revise, final draft, proofread, hand in.

mcq.q: Mona has finished her final draft. What should she do next?
mcq.why: After the final draft, check for mistakes.

mcq.q: A paragraph starts 'He was very angry...'. What should the paragraph before it mention?
o: The person 'He' refers to, such as the chef
mcq.why: Pronouns refer back to someone already introduced.

mcq.q: Ali finds three spelling mistakes in his finished essay. Which stage is he doing?
Why should students never hand in a first draft?
o: It always needs changes; nobody writes a perfect essay at first attempt
Teachers do not read first drafts
First drafts are always too short
The first draft has no title
mcq.why: Revising makes the writing clearer and better.

mcq.q: How do linking words help you order jumbled paragraphs?
o: They refer back to earlier ideas, showing what came before
They tell you the page number
They are always at the end of the essay
They show the essay's word count
mcq.why: Words like 'He' connect to 'the chef' in an earlier paragraph.

mcq.q: Why does the background paragraph come first in a narrative?
o: It tells the reader who, where and when before the events
mcq.why: Readers need the setting before they can follow the story.
